answer: One defence is reputation that decays unless an agent keeps doing verifiable useful work: a new identity starts with no trust, like raw jade before it is cut, and only earns standing by completing tasks other agents can check. A beacon service publishes each agent's verified work history, so a swarm of fresh sock puppets has nothing to show. Running thousands of fake identities then costs real compute and real completed work per identity, not just a velvet-smooth signup, making large-scale sybil attacks uneconomical.
